snapshots.name: Croesus
snapshots.body: King of Lydia, celebrated across the Greek world for his immense wealth. His encounters with Greek sages and his war against a rising Persian power open the Histories' long chain of cause and consequence.

snapshots.name: Solon
snapshots.body: An Athenian lawgiver and sage who visits Croesus's court while traveling abroad. His warning that no man should be called happy until his life is over is one of the work's most quoted exchanges.

snapshots.name: Cyrus
snapshots.body: Founder of the Persian Empire, who rises from a threatened infancy to conquer Media, Lydia, and Babylon in turn. His campaigns establish the Persian power whose later kings dominate the rest of the work.

snapshots.name: Astyages
snapshots.body: The last king of the Medes, whose ominous dreams about his grandson set in motion the chain of events that brings Cyrus to power. His attempt to have the infant Cyrus killed is thwarted before the story properly begins.

snapshots.name: Harpagos
snapshots.body: A Median noble ordered by Astyages to kill the infant Cyrus, who instead has him raised in secret. He later turns against his former king and helps deliver Media into Persian hands.

snapshots.name: Cambyses
snapshots.body: Cyrus's son and successor as king of Persia, who extends his father's conquests into Egypt. His reign is marked, in Herodotus's account, by a growing instability that troubles even his own household.

snapshots.name: Smerdis
snapshots.body: Cambyses's brother, whose name is later claimed by an imposter magus in a plot to seize the Persian throne. The confusion between the true prince and his double becomes a turning point in the succession.

snapshots.name: Dareios
snapshots.body: A Persian noble who becomes king after the death of Cambyses and the exposure of the false Smerdis. His reign organizes the empire into provinces and eventually turns Persian attention toward the Greek mainland.

snapshots.name: Demokedes
snapshots.body: A Greek physician from Croton who rises to prominence at the Persian court after treating Darius's household. His skill wins him privileges rare for a Greek among the Persian elite.

snapshots.name: Polycrates
snapshots.body: Tyrant of Samos, renowned for a run of good fortune so unbroken that even his allies grow uneasy about it. His dealings with Persia's local governor eventually draw the empire's attention to his island.

snapshots.name: Miltiades
snapshots.body: An Athenian commander with experience of Persian affairs from his earlier rule in the Chersonese. He becomes one of the generals responsible for Athens's response to Persia's invasion of Greece.

snapshots.name: Cleomenes
snapshots.body: A king of Sparta known for a forceful, sometimes erratic temperament in both war and diplomacy. His interventions in Athenian and broader Greek politics recur across several episodes of the Histories.

snapshots.name: Demaratos
snapshots.body: A deposed king of Sparta who takes refuge at the Persian court after losing his throne to a rival. His inside knowledge of Greek affairs makes him a valued, if compromised, advisor to the Persian king.

snapshots.name: Xerxes
snapshots.body: Son and successor of Darius, who inherits his father's unfinished plan to punish and conquer Greece. He assembles an enormous invasion force and leads it across the Hellespont in person.

snapshots.name: Artabanos
snapshots.body: Xerxes's uncle and a senior advisor, who counsels caution before the invasion of Greece is launched. His warnings against the scale of the undertaking go largely unheeded by the king.

snapshots.name: Mardonios
snapshots.body: A Persian general and Xerxes's cousin, an ardent advocate for war against the Greeks. He commands Persian forces in the field during the invasion of the Greek mainland.

snapshots.name: Leonidas
snapshots.body: A king of Sparta chosen to lead the Greek defense of a narrow mountain pass against the advancing Persian army. His small force's stand there becomes one of the most famous episodes in the whole work.

snapshots.name: Themistocles
snapshots.body: An Athenian statesman who persuades his city to build the fleet that becomes decisive in the war against Persia. His strategic judgment shapes Greek naval planning through the invasion's critical battles.

snapshots.name: Pausanias
snapshots.body: A Spartan regent given command of the combined Greek land forces late in the war against Persia. His leadership is tested in the campaign that follows the great naval battles of the invasion.

snapshots.name: Datis
snapshots.body: A Median commander placed in charge, alongside a Persian colleague, of an earlier expedition against the Greek mainland. His campaign targets Athens and its ally Eretria directly.

snapshots.name: Gyges
snapshots.body: A Lydian noble whose unusual rise to the throne, recounted early in the Histories, unseats an earlier royal line. His story establishes the dynasty that Croesus will later inherit and lose.
